source_outcome.complete_definition_text: A chemical reaction or transformation of the general type: $$\ce{X-Z + Y -> X-Y-Z}$$ in which the connecting atom or group $\ce{Y}$ replaces the bond joining the parts $\ce{X}$ and $\ce{Z}$ of the reactant $\ce{XZ}$. source_outcome.citation: Citation: 'elimination' in IUPAC Compendium of Chemical Terminology, 5th ed. International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry; 2025. Online version 5.0.0, 2025. 10.1351/goldbook.E02038
source_outcome.complete_definition_text: The reverse of an addition reaction or transformation. In an elimination two groups (called eliminands) are lost most often from two different centres (1/2/elimination or 1/3/elimination, etc.) with concomitant formation of an unsaturation in the molecule (double bond, triple bond) or formation of a new ring. If the groups are lost from a single centre ($\ce{\upalpha\!\mbox{-}elimination}$, 1/1/elimination) the resulting product is a carbene or a 'carbene analogue'.
